sections.content: How many people are "complementary health associate professionals"?

18,925 people

were counted on the census as "complementary health associate professionals" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Complementary health associate professionals use non-mainstream treatments in support of conventional medical treatments.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "complementary health associate professionals" there were more women than men (85.4% compared with 14.6%).

This means "complementary health associate professionals" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "health and social care associate professionals".

Men made up 14.6% and women made up 85.4% of "complementary health associate professionals"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "complementary health associate professionals" included:

  • human resources administrative occupations
  • special and additional needs education teaching professionals
  • health care practice managers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "complementary health associate professionals", 15.8% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "complementary health associate professionals" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "complementary health associate professionals" included:

  • chief executives and senior officials
  • production managers and directors in manufacturing
  • directors in logistics, warehousing and transport

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "complementary health associate professionals", 14.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (79.4% compared with 20.6%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (85.7%) than an employee (14.3%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Cornwall, this is in the region of the South West.
